claims.text: Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in HEAs is governed by the stability of passivating oxide layers.
Multi-elemental composition enhances the stability of passivating oxide layers.
Lattice distortion enhances the stability of passivating oxide layers.
The proposed initial HEA has a homogeneous microstructure.
The proposed initial HEA has a stable passivating oxide layer.
Systematically varying HEA elemental composition will alter the composition of the passivating oxide layer.
Systematically varying HEA elemental composition will alter the stability of the passivating oxide layer.
The multi-elemental composition of HEAs promotes formation of a chemically stable passivating oxide layer.
The multi-elemental composition of HEAs promotes formation of a mechanically robust passivating oxide layer.
A chemically stable and mechanically robust oxide layer resists mechanical disruption during wear.
An oxide layer that resists mechanical disruption maintains corrosion resistance under simultaneous mechanical and chemical stresses.
HEA compositions that enhance oxide-layer stability will have lower combined degradation rates than alloys with less stable oxide layers.
HEA compositions that enhance oxide-layer stability will have lower wear rates.
HEA compositions that enhance oxide-layer stability will have lower corrosion rates.
The conventional-alloy baseline has a simpler composition than the tested HEAs.
The conventional-alloy baseline has a less stable passivating oxide layer under the test conditions.
The prediction requires sufficient lattice distortion and multi-elemental synergy to form stable oxide layers.
The prediction may fail for HEA compositions that do not support passivating oxide formation.
The prediction may fail in environments that prevent oxide-layer formation.
Highly reducing conditions can prevent formation of the relevant oxide layer.
